races.name: Close Brothers Asset Finance Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Pride Of Nepal
runners_data.note: Three wins in five starts at 10-12f on good ground make this trip and conditions spot-on; Charlie Tucker (7lb claimer) is a mild concern for Tony Carroll's stable that has shown strong 14-day form (5/31), and the horse's hold-up style is genuine and suits a race where Harlington could set it up.|
runners_data.comment: Seventh last time out, but that was bracketed by two similar efforts either side of a red-hot run of four straight wins beforehand. Quick to reappear just eight days on and has run over today's trip before; a middle-of-the-road claim on a rating of 69.

runners_data.name: Harlington
runners_data.note: Charlie Clover's five-year-old has won three times at 10f on standard/tapeta and carries a STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) suggesting it is slightly out of its most comfortable role as a lead horse at this track and trip; Liam Wright takes over and the horse should get its lead unchallenged, which is the key variable its chance hinges on.|
runners_data.comment: An eighth last time out looks the odd one out after a pair of thirds, with a hot streak of three straight wins further back again showing real depth to the form. Has run over today's trip before and sits second on our figures at 75, with that recent blip the one query.

runners_data.name: Imperial Cult
runners_data.note: George Baker's seven-year-old won over 11f and 12f on standard ground recently, suggesting the step back to 12f turf on good is no issue; Jack Callan takes the ride and the trainer's 14-day record (0/6) is flat, but prominent running style should see it slot comfortably into second or third behind Harlington.|
runners_data.comment: A fourth last time out follows back-to-back wins two and three starts back, with two thirds further back again — a strong recent trend. Has run over today's trip before and sits third on our figures at 71, with that closing fourth the only blot.

runners_data.name: King's Castle
runners_data.note: David Simcock's nine-year-old has strong place form at 12f on good ground (5W7P similar going) and Taryn Langley's 3lb claim is useful; 40 days off is the query, but prominent style means it will be ideally positioned in the race's natural shape, and course form over the trip is exactly what the scenario favours.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in its last five starts but rarely below halfway, with a second and two thirds showing real consistency. Ten pounds clear of its current official mark of 66, tops our figures at 76, and has run over today's trip before despite six weeks off.

runners_data.name: Golden Phase
runners_data.note: Denis Coakley's six-year-old is a natural prominent racer with three wins on good ground over 10f but has been off 232 days — a serious fitness concern; Rose Dawes picks up the ride, and though the horse is displaced to midfield on the map due to crowding at the front, its best form was made racing close to the pace rather than from off it, tempering confidence if it cannot get forward.|
runners_data.comment: A winner three starts back and rarely far off before that, with a second and two thirds either side. Has run over today's trip before, sits fourth on our figures at 70, but a 232-day absence since a blank effort last time out is the obvious worry.

runners_data.name: Symphony's Song
runners_data.note: Ian Williams's four-year-old is stepping up sharply in trip from 8f, with no form beyond that distance and only one run on comparable going; Toby Moore (7lb claimer) is aboard and the 17-day turnaround is fine, but the hold-up style and unproven stamina make this a speculative runner at best.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in its last four starts, finishing fifth, fourth, sixth and fourth in that run — modest, unimproving form. Race fit after just 17 days off, but bottom of our figures at 59 in a field of seven, with others clearly preferred.

runners_data.name: Mrembo
runners_data.note: Jonathan Portman's mare has won over 12f on good ground at Sandown and Olivia Tubb (3lb claim) is a positive; a true hold-up type whose position on the map understates how far back she will likely race — STYLE_FIT (0.91) flags she may not get back as far as she ideally wants in a small field, and 23 days between runs is routine for her.|
runners_data.comment: A winner three starts back, sandwiched between two fourths, with a third and two fifths elsewhere in a modest recent record. Has run over today's trip before but is second-bottom on our figures at 65, only three weeks on from its last outing.

races.paceDynamic: Harlington is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should slide into an uncontested, controlled position from the gate at Sandown's 1m2f start. The pace will be honest but entirely on Harlington's terms — a sustainable gallop that is unlikely to be truly searching given the absence of any horse willing to press from the outside. Imperial Cult and King's Castle are the most credible prominent racers likely to shadow Harlington in second and third, shaping a race where the front two or three control tempo and the closers face a stiff final climb to Sandown's line on ground that remains unknown but is nominally described as good. This race shape most favours hold-up horses with proven finishing kicks over this trip, particularly Pride Of Nepal whose strong recent record at 12f on good ground is tailor-made, though the controlled pace is a double-edged sword — if Harlington conserves energy and quickens, prominent types who travel close to the pace gain the edge. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural positions; Golden Phase and Mrembo are genuine prominent and hold-up types respectively displaced to midfield on the map, with Imperial Cult and King's Castle most likely to actually lock in the prominent slots behind Harlington.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Harlington Controls, Front Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Harlington leads unchallenged at a controlled pace and the Sandown climb does not fully unwind the advantage.
scenarios.body: Harlington dictates every yard, setting a tempo that suits those travelling close to the pace, and the stiff finish rewards horses who have conserved energy in behind rather than those charging from the back; the front two or three deny the closers enough time to reel them in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to soften the front end and Pride Of Nepal's proven 12f finishing kick can be deployed.
scenarios.body: Pride Of Nepal's six-run form string including three recent wins, all on good ground at 10-12f, positions it perfectly for a strong late run up the Sandown hill if the leaders have gone hard enough to tire.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Pivot Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is moderate and a horse tracking in mid-division times a run perfectly off the turn.
scenarios.body: Golden Phase, though mapped to midfield out of its natural prominent role, has course-relevant good-ground form and could benefit if it finds a clear passage to mount a challenge from a handy position at the two-furlong pole.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Collapses Into Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the pace completely stalls, the field concertinas and the race is decided by a sprint finish from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Symphony's Song, stepping up from shorter trips, is an unknown quantity at 1m2f but a flat-out dash from a tight group could theoretically suit a horse whose short-distance speed remains unexploited at this trip.

watchPoints.text: Harlington's uncontested lead is the race's central variable — if anything pressures it early, the entire pace dynamic changes and hold-up horses gain significantly.|

Golden Phase's 232-day absence is a significant fitness flag; watch how it moves in the preliminaries and whether it travels freely in the early stages, as a ring-rusty effort could block runners trying to mount challenges.|

Pride Of Nepal's hold-up style in a small seven-runner field risks finding no cover and being drawn into a position further forward than ideal — watch the early stages to see if Charlie Tucker can hold it back.|

Symphony's Song is unproven beyond 8f; if it travels strongly into the Sandown straight it is worth noting as a form revelation over the trip, but a weakening display from the home turn would confirm the stamina question.|
King's Castle has the joint-highest similar-going place count in the field (5W7P) but has not run for 40 days — monitor market moves from David Simcock's yard as a guide to fitness confidence.|

races.name: Chasemore Farm EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Close Brothers Premium Finance Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Appier
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer who shapes as the chief beneficiary of an uncontested Personal Best-led pace; handles Good going and has winning form over 1m+ staying trips, though 42 days off and a poor recent run at Goodwood 1m6f on Good needs noting — trainer Carroll has modest 14-day strike rate.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, rounding off a mixed six-run stretch that also contained a sixth and an unplaced effort alongside three runs in the frame. Has run over today's trip before and sits second on our figures at 82, though six weeks have passed since that win.

runners_data.name: Personal Best
runners_data.note: Sole front runner here and likely to have it all its own way up front; Jason Watson partnership with Portman is solid, handles Good going well (5 placed from 12 similar-going runs), but the STYLE_FIT tag reminds that this horse is racing somewhat against its natural instincts as a prominent type asked to fully lead — discount if it cannot handle total isolation.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in its last five starts but ultra-consistent, with three seconds, a third and a fourth showing it barely runs a bad race. Has run over today's trip before and tops our figures at 84, a clear step up on its current official mark of 79.

runners_data.name: Knight Templar
runners_data.note: 121 days off is a significant flag for a horse whose best form has come fresh at this trip on Good going at Sandown and similar; Robert Stephens has 0 from 2 in the 14-day window suggesting yard not firing at peak, but course form (won 1m6f Good) gives it residual claims if fit.
runners_data.comment: A winner four starts back but that was followed by a flat eighth, before finding form again with back-to-back seconds. Has run over today's trip before and sits fourth on our figures at 78, though a lengthy 121-day absence is the concern this time.

runners_data.name: Ludo's Landing
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's yard is excellent (3/54 in 14 days is volume-driven) and this hold-up type carries the hood (b) which may sharpen focus; 30 days since last run is fine, though six runs at today's 1m6f trip show mixed finishing positions — benefits directly from a steady Personal Best-led tempo.
runners_data.comment: A winner five starts back, with a third two starts ago among a mixed set of efforts since. Has run over today's trip before and is fit again just 30 days on from a fifth last time out, with our figures rating it 81.

runners_data.name: Laravie
runners_data.note: Arrives in blistering form — five consecutive top-two finishes including three wins on similar Going — but its genuine prominence means it has been redistributed to midfield in this map because the race has insufficient room for all pace-inclined types; the visor (v) aids concentration, and Luke Morris will try to recover position, though the STYLE_FIT discount tempers confidence.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in a row from three to five starts back and two seconds since round off a strong sequence, with the yard among the in-form. Has run over today's trip before, but a modest speed figure leaves it fifth on our figures at 74.

runners_data.name: Mister Daydream
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse in natural terms, though mapped to midfield as a positional redistribution artefact; arrives on an 11-day turnaround which is short but Moore's yard has recent form; winning record at 1m2f is shorter than today's 1m6f, raising a stamina question over this staying trip.
runners_data.comment: A winner two starts back, following a flat two-run spell of sevenths, with a second again last time out. Has run over today's trip before and returns quickly, just 11 days on, but is bottom of our figures at 74.

races.paceDynamic: Personal Best is the lone confirmed front runner and, with no genuine challenger pressing for the lead, will dictate a controlled, even gallop over this 1m6f trip at Sandown. Knight Templar is also prominent in style but has been off 121 days and is unlikely to forcefully dispute the early lead, meaning Personal Best should stride clear and set whatever tempo suits. The field contains more pace-inclined horses than the map can accommodate — Laravie is a genuine prominent racer who will be squeezed into midfield by circumstance, while Mister Daydream, a natural hold-up type, is similarly mapped out of its ideal position. A sedate, munsurprising pace set by an uncontested Personal Best over a staying trip on Good turf is a recipe that strongly favours genuine, uncomplicated hold-up closers who can pick up ground from the rear in the straight, with Appier and Ludo's Landing best-placed tactically to benefit.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Personal Best leads at a steady clip and the field strings out, allowing true closers to pick up into the straight.
scenarios.body: Personal Best's uncontested lead over 1m6f creates a one-paced tempo that leaves plenty of fuel in the tank of those held up, who can produce a sustained finish into the Sandown straight. Appier and Ludo's Landing, both natural hold-up horses with stamina to call on, are best suited to swoop late as the pace honest but never punishing.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Knight Templar recovers full fitness quickly off 121 days and pushes Personal Best, resulting in both pulling clear before the home straight.
scenarios.body: A stiffer pace set by two prominent types suits horses who can travel prominently themselves and respond to a quickening challenge, rather than those needing the race truly run to suit a late rattle. Knight Templar's course form over 1m6f on Good going is strong, and if he hits the line running, he and Personal Best could prove too good for the closers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistributed Laravie Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Laravie, a genuinely prominent horse, is able to force its way nearer the pace than the map suggests and produce its recent form.
scenarios.body: Laravie arrives in career-best form with six wins and eight places from 15 runs on similar going, and if the race develops slowly enough to allow a forward move, its natural cruising speed could make it competitive. However, being pushed out of its natural position reduces the likelihood of it executing fully, and the STYLE_FIT discount applies here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Tests Hold-Ups
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or Personal Best is reeled in early, creating a tactical vacuum that tests every horse's resolution.
scenarios.body: An unpredictable tempo with no clear rail to the finish suits those able to quicken from varying positions, but Mister Daydream — a genuine hold-up type shuffled into midfield — risks being caught in no-man's land and unable to produce its best. Appier, with proven stamina at staying trips, holds the most residual value even in a messy scenario.

watchPoints.text: Personal Best sets an uncontested lead — if Jason Watson is allowed to stride clear at his own pace, watch how far he stretches the field by halfway, as an early gap could be fatal to the hold-up horses.

Knight Templar's 121-day absence is the biggest unknown in the race — if he bounces out to dispute the lead with Personal Best, the tempo lifts sharply and the complexion of the race changes for everyone behind.

Laravie's rider Luke Morris will attempt to push forward from its drawn position to recapture natural prominent ground; if that move succeeds, watch for it creeping into the frame despite the redistribution concern.
Mister Daydream at only 11 days since last run and stepping up markedly in trip from 1m2f — monitor in the paddock and watch how it handles the Sandown climb if it gets detached at the rear early.

Ludo's Landing is fitted with a hood today — watch its behaviour in preliminaries and early strides, as headgear changes at Sandown over this trip can either sharpen or unsettle a horse on its first use.

races.name: Close Brothers Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Cyrano De Bergerac
runners_data.note: Recent course-winning form at 10f on good going is the standout angle here; John & Thady Gosden's yard is firing (8 from 19 over 14 days) and Luke Catton's 3lb claim is a genuine weight-saving bonus over identical OR rivals — sits naturally close to the pace and the step up from 10f appears already proven.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out having been runner-up in each of its previous two starts — clear improvement with the form still on an upward curve. Has run over today's trip before and is fourth on our figures at 80, though its sample is still just three runs.

runners_data.name: Hot And Cold
runners_data.note: A notable trip and class rise from winning at 8f; Sir Mark Prescott horses rarely turn up underprepared at 13 days, but the jump to 10f on a track that stretches stamina is a real question — the STYLE_FIT flag notes this horse may not race as prominently as its role implies, which subtly tempers confidence in its ability to dictate fully.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins two and three starts back followed a pair of below-par efforts, and a good second last time out confirms the improvement has stuck. Fit again quickly after just 13 days and clear on our figures at 90, nine pounds up on its official mark of 81.

runners_data.name: Knightsail
runners_data.note: Jamie Spencer's patient hold-up style suits a closer, but the 107-day absence for David Menuisier's yard (0 from 6 in the 14-day window) is a concern; best recent run was a third at 9f on good, and the race shape here looks likely to punish horses who need a strong pace injection late.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in its last three starts but a third sandwiched between two sevenths hints at ability, and second on our figures at 82. Has run over today's trip before, but a 107-day absence since that effort is the big query.

runners_data.name: Blue Noon
runners_data.note: Consistent at this trip — four of five runs have been at 10f on good ground, placing twice — and Richard Hannon's yard is active (7 from 56 in 14 days); Sean Levey knows this horse well, but a win has remained elusive and the horse's style is unclear (listed Unknown), making its place in the tactical picture hard to pin down.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in its last five starts but rarely below fourth, with a third last time out the pick of a consistent recent sequence. Has run over today's trip before and sits third on our figures at 80, with a dip to sixth two starts back the exception.

runners_data.name: Roker Roar
runners_data.note: The 184-day absence is the dominant factor here; Andrew Balding's yard is in form (13 from 54) but Roker Roar has no win and no place from three runs on good ground, and asking a horse returning from six months off to peg back a well-positioned rival over 1m2f is a big ask regardless of the pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: A third last time out capped a steady improvement from a seventh two starts before that. Has run over today's trip before, but a lengthy 184-day absence since and bottom spot on our figures at 66 leave plenty to prove.

races.paceDynamic: Hot And Cold is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only five runners on a flat 1m2f Sandown track, will be able to bowl along at a comfortable, uncontested tempo. Cyrano De Bergerac maps as a prominent type and is the likeliest to sit just behind Hot And Cold in second position, creating a natural two-horse lead group with the remainder strung behind. The pace is unlikely to be truly searching — a solo leader who meets no pressure can control fractions and deliver a stamina-conserving gallop that blunts the advantage of deep closers. This race shape strongly favours a horse that can travel handily close to the pace, since a slow-to-modest tempo over 1m2f will compress the finish and make it very difficult for the genuine hold-up horses Knightsail and Roker Roar to generate the momentum required to run down a well-positioned rival.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Hot And Cold bowls along without any pressure and the pace remains steady throughout.
scenarios.body: Hot And Cold dictates every yard, conserving energy through the middle section before quickening away inside the final two furlongs; a horse tracking closely in second — Cyrano De Bergerac — is ideally positioned to challenge or inherit the lead without burning extra energy. Prominent racers who sit within two lengths of the pace are the primary beneficiaries as they never have to switch off or make up ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Finish Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the lead duo of Hot And Cold and Cyrano De Bergerac combine to dominate from the front and the hold-up horses have too much ground to make up.
scenarios.body: The steady gallop leaves Knightsail and Roker Roar without the strong pace injection they need to close, and the front two simply grind it out between themselves in the closing stages. Cyrano De Bergerac's recent win at 10f on good ground gives him a course-trip profile edge over Hot And Cold, who is stepping up noticeably from his habitual 8f trips.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Exploit Slow Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If the pace set by Hot And Cold is genuinely too modest and the hold-up horses time their runs to sweep past a flattening leader.
scenarios.body: A crawl over the first mile would theoretically compress the field and give Knightsail and Roker Roar a sprint-home scenario, though both are 107 and 184 days off the course respectively, which is a significant fitness concern. Blue Noon, who has shown consistent form at this trip and distance on good ground, is better placed than the others to take advantage if the front two tire.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Hold-Up Winner
scenarios.trigger: If a hold-up horse is significantly ahead of the market on fitness or ability and the pace collapses entirely in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Roker Roar, off 184 days and without a win at this trip on good ground, represents the longest shot at capitalising; Knightsail showed a placed effort at 9f on good and would need the race to truly fall apart at the front. Both face the dual hurdle of long lay-offs and a tactical scenario that demands near-perfect sectionals from a small field.

watchPoints.text: Hot And Cold is the pace-anchor for this race — watch whether it jumps cleanly and moves forward immediately, because any hesitation or reluctance to lead would remove the only confirmed pace-setter and leave the fractions completely undefined.

Knightsail and Roker Roar are both returning from significant absences (107 and 184 days respectively) — if either appears to be moving poorly in the pre-race canter or show any race-rustiness in the early stages, discount their chance of getting competitive from off the pace.

Cyrano De Bergerac carries top weight alongside Hot And Cold at 136lbs — watch how comfortably Luke Catton holds his position in the first half-mile, as any sign of pulling or fighting for the bit early would be a red flag on the climb to the home straight.

Blue Noon's running style is recorded as Unknown — watch where Sean Levey positions the horse in the first two furlongs to understand whether it will contest the prominent berths or settle further back, as this will define its route into the race entirely.

races.name: Close Brothers Invoice Finance Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Winston's Warrior
runners_data.note: Charles Hills has this four-year-old in good nick (2/18 in 14 days) and he has won twice at this trip and similar going, but his natural style is prominent rather than front-running — the STYLE_FIT flag tempers how reliably he can convert if forced to lead flat out; 13 days since last run is fine.
runners_data.comment: A winner three and five starts back either side of a third, but that form has cooled with an eighth and a fifth since. Has run over today's trip before and returns quickly after just 13 days, rated 85 by us — the recent dip is the query.

runners_data.name: Cristo
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon has a solid runner here with two wins and four places from 15 starts on comparable going; a genuine prominent racer with a strong record over 8f on good ground, and Sean Levey's booking adds confidence — the headgear note (p) suggests he needs an honest gallop to be seen at his best.
runners_data.comment: A winner two starts back and a good second last time out show the form is trending the right way after an unseated interruption a few starts ago. Has run over today's trip before and tops our figures at 89, a few pounds clear of the rest.

runners_data.name: Sea Suite
runners_data.note: James Owen's five-time good-ground runner has won and placed repeatedly at 7-8f on going to suit, and the visor (v) sharpens her hold-up style; Luke Morris retains the ride for a trainer in 13/38 form over 14 days, and 9 days since last run is no concern — her natural closer profile is perfectly aligned with the expected race shape.
runners_data.comment: A winner three starts back but a below-par seventh followed, before bouncing back with a second last time out. Has run over today's trip before, races from a yard in good form, and carries a strong speed figure of 83 despite sitting fifth on our figures at 80.

runners_data.name: Bubbles Wonky
runners_data.note: Mark Pattinson has a 0/4 14-day record and the 65-day absence is the most significant flag here; genuinely a hold-up horse whose position on the map reflects the crowded rear of the field rather than any change in style — all five recent runs are on Southwell's all-weather, making this turf reappearance on good ground a notable unknown.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in its last five starts but the trend is emphatically the right way, from a ninth to back-to-back thirds. Has run over today's trip before and a big speed figure of 83 backs up fourth on our figures at 82, despite 65 days off since.

runners_data.name: Lorca's Waltz
runners_data.note: William Haggas's three-year-old won over this exact course, distance and going in her most recent start — a compelling form fact — and a tongue tie (t) suggests connections have addressed a breathing concern; Cieren Fallon rides for a stable with a respectable 4/46 fortnight strike rate, and 38 days since that course win is entirely manageable for a lightly-raced filly.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, a big improvement on a ninth and a fifth in its two starts before that. Has run over today's trip before, but a wide gap between its rating of 65 with us and an official mark of 79 leaves it bottom of this field.

runners_data.name: Swiped
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old has a sharp recent record of 1-2-1-2 and two wins on good ground over a mile, but is a genuine prominent racer who has been pushed back on the map due to positional crowding — Rhys Clutterbuck takes over from a stronger jockey pool and the STYLE_FIT discount applies if she cannot secure her natural tracking position; the visor (v) is retained.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out to cap a strong run of a second, a win and a second across its previous four starts, backed by a yard in good order. Has run over today's trip before and sits third on our figures at 83, with a modest speed figure the one query.

races.paceDynamic: Winston's Warrior is the lone confirmed front runner here and looks set to dictate from the front unchallenged, which should translate into a controlled, honest gallop rather than a searching test. Cristo and Swiped are both naturally prominent horses, meaning there will be competition for early positions behind the leader, though with one runner able to stride clear, the pace is unlikely to be truly severe. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all achieve their natural position — Swiped and Bubbles Wonky are both redistributed on the map, with Cristo and Winston's Warrior best placed to secure the early slots ahead of them. This shape — a single unchallenged leader setting a sustainable tempo — strongly favours hold-up and late-finishing profiles who can track a steady pace and produce a sustained run, with Sea Suite and Lorca's Waltz ideally positioned by style to exploit a race run at an honest but not punishing gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Leader, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Winston's Warrior leads uncontested at a sustainable gallop, setting up a straight-line sprint finish.
scenarios.body: The controlled tempo allows the prominent horses to travel comfortably in behind while the true hold-up types get a clean run through; the Sandown straight rewards those who finish strongly. Sea Suite and Lorca's Waltz, both genuine hold-up types with strong good-ground form, are ideally suited to pounce once the steady pace is exposed in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Control
scenarios.trigger: If Cristo tracks Winston's Warrior closely and the pair dominate the race from the front, preventing any meaningful hold-up run.
scenarios.body: A two-horse show up front could produce a strong, even gallop that plays into the hands of those racing close to the pace, with Cristo's strong record on good ground over this trip making him a logical beneficiary. Winston's Warrior has already won twice at 8f on standout ground and could hold on if the tempo is just right to suit his cruising speed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Outrun Field
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is faster than expected, burning off the prominent horses and leaving the field strung out for a true staying finish.
scenarios.body: A genuine test of stamina through the Sandown mile would expose those who have raced prominently throughout and reward any runner able to switch off and produce a late run; Sea Suite's visored headgear and hold-up profile make her the primary beneficiary. Lorca's Waltz, a winner over this course and distance on good ground, has the class and tactical profile to capitalise if the pace collapses in front of her.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Chaos Intervenes
scenarios.trigger: If traffic problems or interference in a small six-runner field disrupt the natural race shape and compress the finish.
scenarios.body: A tight field can still produce bunching into the Sandown straight if early positions are contested by the redistributed prominent horses jostling for berths; any runner getting a clean passage late could benefit. Swiped, though mapped to midfield due to redistribution and racing out of natural role, has two wins on good ground at a mile and could prove dangerous if she finds daylight.

watchPoints.text: Winston's Warrior leads alone on a going-unknown surface — if he finds a very easy opening, the pace could be slower than expected, sharply compressing the final-furlong sprint and favouring Sea Suite and Lorca's Waltz over any prominent horse trying to sustain an effort.

Swiped and Cristo are both naturally prominent horses competing for the same early slots behind Winston's Warrior — watch for either to be squeezed back or forced wide exiting the stalls, which would leave them racing out of their best position and reduce their effectiveness late.

Bubbles Wonky's 65-day absence, combined with an all-weather form profile being tested on good turf for the first time in this sample, makes her difficult to assess — any market move late should be noted as trainer intent, given the low 0/4 14-day stable strike rate.

Lorca's Waltz is the only runner with a win at this exact course and distance on matching going in her most recent start — watch whether Cieren Fallon positions her to track the pace through the final bend rather than being held up wide, as Sandown's camber can make wide draws costly late.

races.name: Close Brothers Motor Finance Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Lyra Lea
runners_data.note: Confirmed lone front-runner for Rod Millman who gets a golden opportunity to dictate unchallenged; best recent form came on good ground at 7f and she goes well fresh at 24 days, though the STYLE_FIT flag suggests some risk if the race shape demands something more of her.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out and two starts back, with a further placed effort four starts back, this filly is admirably consistent without a win in her last five starts. Top-rated on our figures, with trip experience and a yard in good form; the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Decalogue
runners_data.note: Jamie Osborne's hold-up performer has a worrying tendency to fade in the finish, and three recent runs all ended in 6th-8th — the lack of any placed effort in three starts and 58 days off since last seen makes it hard to construct a winning scenario.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in each of his last three starts, including eighth last time out, and without a win in that spell, he's bottom of our ratings here. A 58-day break and trip experience offer little encouragement against this field.

runners_data.name: Unionville
runners_data.note: Kieren Fox partners a horse whose best work has come over 6f on standard ground, stepping up to 7f on good at Sandown; won on standard and placed at 6f but the two runs on slower or longer trips produced 7th and 8th, so trip and going combination are both slight queries.
runners_data.comment: A winner four starts back and runner-up before that, this gelding has solid earlier form and trip experience. He's since faded to two eighth-placed efforts, the obvious concern, but the deeper formline puts him among the leading dangers here.

runners_data.name: Berkshire Boom
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's runner is the most interesting held-up/prominent profile in the race — a winner over 7f on good ground and placed twice in similar conditions — and Jason Watson, a capable race-reader, can position him just behind Lyra Lea and deliver a clean challenge inside the last.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out, and third two starts back, this gelding is in good recent form with trip experience. A win five starts back and just 14 days since his last run point to a sharp contender, with the two moderate efforts sandwiched between the only blot.

runners_data.name: Norfolk Blue
runners_data.note: William Knight's colt is a genuine hold-up horse pushed into the midfield map slot purely because the field has too many closers for the display; his best form includes a placed effort over 7f on good, but the STYLE_FIT tag and redistribution both temper expectations of him getting a clean run from his natural position.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up two starts back is the standout form, either side of which he's found only mid-table finishes, without a win in his last five starts. He has trip experience and sits fourth on our figures, but needs to rediscover that effort to trouble those above him.

runners_data.name: King Cherry
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams sends out a lightly raced three-year-old wearing a tongue-tie on return from 70 days off; three runs have produced 5th, 7th, and 8th, and like Norfolk Blue his true hold-up style is displaced on this map — too many hold-up types, too few closers' lanes at Sandown's uphill finish.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in each of his last three starts and without a win in that spell, this gelding also returns from a lengthy 70-day break. Trip experience is the one thing in his favour, but he's second-bottom on our figures and hard to fancy on this form.

races.paceDynamic: Lyra Lea is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she should dictate from the front at a measured, controlled tempo over this 7f at Sandown. Berkshire Boom will press prominently just behind, but the four hold-up horses — Decalogue, Unionville, Norfolk Blue, and King Cherry — will need to settle in behind a pace that may simply not be fast enough to stretch the race out for them. Norfolk Blue and King Cherry are genuine hold-up types pushed forward on the map because the field is backloaded with closers; they are unlikely to secure anything like a natural front position and will likely be shuffled even further back than displayed. The race shape strongly favours the prominent-to-front profile: Lyra Lea controlling from the front and Berkshire Boom tracking in a position to pounce, with the hold-up brigade relying on a pace scenario that this lone front-runner is unlikely to deliver.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lyra Lea Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Lyra Lea leads comfortably at a sustainable gallop and is not pushed into an unsustainable pace, the race becomes a waiting exercise for those behind.
scenarios.body: Lyra Lea dictates every yard, setting a rhythm that suits herself and the tracking Berkshire Boom, with the hold-up runners running out of ground on the testing Sandown 7f finish. Prominent racers who can get into a challenging position at the two-furlong pole are best placed to capitalise.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Berkshire Boom Challenges Late
scenarios.trigger: If Berkshire Boom tracks Lyra Lea closely in second and produces a sustained challenge inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Andrew Balding's runner has solid form over this trip on good ground — five of his six career runs at 7f or similar — and Jason Watson can time a run from just off the leader's shoulder. Lyra Lea gets caught by a fresher closer who has the class edge at the weights.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or Lyra Lea overcooks it under pressure, leaving a gap for the true closers to swoop late.
scenarios.body: Unionville has winning form on good-ish ground over shorter and could benefit from a strong pace, while Norfolk Blue has hit the frame on good ground at 7f before. However, both are genuine hold-up types mapped out of position, making this scenario reliant on an unlikely pace collapse from an uncontested front-runner.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Compressed Finish, Any Winner
scenarios.trigger: If pace is so slow that the entire field bunches at the two-furlong pole and it becomes a sprint from the front.
scenarios.body: A falsely run race at a crawl could theoretically bring King Cherry and Decalogue into contention, but both have poor recent form and King Cherry is stepping up significantly in class with only three career runs. This scenario requires a race shape that defies everything the pace map points toward.

watchPoints.text: Lyra Lea sets an uncontested pace — watch whether she is allowed to coast in front or whether Berkshire Boom's rider pushes her into a faster gallop that could compromise her finishing effort.
Norfolk Blue and King Cherry are genuine hold-up horses shown in midfield on the map — watch for both to drift back toward the rear early, which would put them out of the frame if the pace is slow.
Decalogue's tendency to fade in the finish combined with 58 days off is a red flag — watch for any early signs of greenness or sluggishness that confirm he is not ready to fire.

Berkshire Boom returns on a 14-day turnaround for Balding, who has a strong 13/54 strike rate in the 14-day window — watch for him to be produced with maximum purpose under Watson in the final two furlongs.
